title: Over How Many Segments a Cabin Move Is Taken on a Return Air Ticket Fare Brands Booking
content:
On an Air Ticket Fare Brands booking that carries a return date, the segments a move into a higher cabin is taken over are measured off the booking's own fare lines rather than assumed.

## 1. The measure

1.1 Where a return date stands on the booking and its fare lines run to more than 1 segment, the move is taken over every segment the fare lines run to.

1.2 Where a return date stands on the booking and its fare lines run to a single segment, the move is taken over the 2 directions of the journey.

1.3 In every other case no such re-measure is made.

The segment count read is the highest segment position reached by the fare lines standing on the booking. Both of the first two rows open on a return date standing on the booking, so a one-way booking never falls on either.

## 2. Condition matrix

| Return date on the booking | Segments the fare lines run to | Segments the move is taken over |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | more than 1 | every segment the fare lines run to |
| yes | a single segment | 2 |
| no | any | no such re-measure |

## 3. Worked readings, on hypothetical figures

A return booking whose fare lines reach a fourth segment: the move is taken over 4 segments.

A return booking whose fare lines were posted as a single segment covering the whole journey: the fare lines do not run to more than 1 segment, so the move is taken over the 2 directions of the journey.

A one-way booking whose fare lines reach a third segment: no such re-measure is made, whatever the fare lines show.
